domain_hypothesis.reasoning: The dataset contains columns typical of e-commerce retail transactions: InvoiceNo (transaction identifier), StockCode and Description (product details), Quantity and UnitPrice (order line items), InvoiceDate (transaction timestamp), CustomerID (buyer identifier), and Country (geographic market). The presence of these fields strongly suggests a retail sales domain.

kpi_specs.name: Total Revenue
kpi_specs.description: Sum of all sales revenue (Quantity * UnitPrice) across all transactions, providing a high-level measure of business performance.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT SUM(Quantity * UnitPrice) AS total_revenue FROM data
kpi_specs.reasoning: Total revenue is a fundamental KPI for retail businesses, and a single summary number is best displayed as a card.

kpi_specs.name: Revenue by Country
kpi_specs.description: Total revenue broken down by Country, identifying top markets and regional performance.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT Country, SUM(Quantity * UnitPrice) AS revenue FROM data GROUP BY Country ORDER BY revenue DESC
kpi_specs.reasoning: Country is a low-cardinality categorical dimension, making it ideal for a bar chart to compare revenue across regions.

kpi_specs.name: Monthly Revenue Trend
kpi_specs.description: Total revenue aggregated by month to analyze sales trends over time.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', InvoiceDate) AS month, SUM(Quantity * UnitPrice) AS revenue FROM data GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
kpi_specs.reasoning: A line chart is the best way to visualize trends over time, and InvoiceDate allows for monthly aggregation.

kpi_specs.name: Top 10 Products by Revenue
kpi_specs.description: The 10 products (StockCode) generating the highest revenue, highlighting best-selling items.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT StockCode, Description, SUM(Quantity * UnitPrice) AS revenue FROM data GROUP BY StockCode, Description ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 10
kpi_specs.reasoning: A bar chart effectively ranks products by revenue, and StockCode/Description are suitable dimensions for this comparison.

kpi_specs.name: Customer Purchase Frequency
kpi_specs.description: Number of invoices per customer, identifying how often customers make purchases.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT CustomerID, COUNT(DISTINCT InvoiceNo) AS invoice_count FROM data WHERE CustomerID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY CustomerID ORDER BY invoice_count DESC
kpi_specs.reasoning: A table is appropriate here due to the high cardinality of CustomerID and the need to display exact counts for analysis.
